fields.v: No SDD approach. CoReMem (Coding-Repository Memory): (M1) prospective segment valuation yielding a memory template built on 'anchors' (repository locations and executable checks); (M2) cost-internalizing on-policy post-training (reward charges steps inside success); (M3) provenance-gated value credit. 'CoReMem w/o training' = memory on frozen actor. Version: N/A

Memory.md written by the actor at the end of each task, before the next task is known: task block (STATUS, TESTS with exit codes, VERIFY commands, DID/WHERE/FILES) and repository block (CONTEXT, WHERE: layout and how to test); reasoning text and scratch files dropped. Keeps the median step saving of the full trajectory with 6% of its bytes

fields.v: Tasks: ChainSWE test half (48 chains, 96 boundaries), disjoint repositories from training. Configurations: 7 memory conditions x 3 open-weight actors (post-trained) + 6 conditions x 3 API actors (frozen). Baseline: no memory on same actor. Held constant: harness (mini-swe-agent), window, step limits per model, memory-layer official instructions. Repetitions: replays 12 (9B frozen), 6-7 (27B), 6 (DeepSeek), 3 (Gemma, Luna), 1 (Opus). Checkpoint rule fixed in advance. Human intervention: none

CoReMem w/o training lowers steps on all six actors (significantly on three, by 9-13%) without lowering resolution (rises on five, unchanged on Opus), total tokens within -7% to +5% of no memory on five of six; Mem0/MemOp/ReasoningBank cost more tokens than CoReMem w/o training on five of six (and more than no memory on all six: +13% to +127%). Post-trained CoReMem vs no memory on the untrained actor: steps lower on all three (by up to 26%: -26% 9B, -17% 27B, -5% Gemma), total tokens -9% to -19%, resolution +22% to +27% relative, resolve per total token +38% to +46% (avg 41%); against the same memory on the untrained actor steps fall a further 24% (9B) and 8% (27B). 27B frozen memory: resolve 21.3% -> 23.4% (+2.1 [+0.4, +3.7]). Significance via paired chain-cluster bootstrap 95% intervals

rev.why: r1 gave post-trained steps as -17% to -26%; Gemma's post-trained steps fall only 5% (Table 1, p. 7; text says 'by up to 26%'). Added the further step drop against the untrained actor with memory (p. 8)

fields.v: Distinguished memory layers on effort (steps, tokens); resolution differences small, intervals sometimes include zero; replays vary by model (1 for Opus). Generalisation checks on SWE-bench Verified, two external chain benchmarks and OpenHands harness

Main experiments on Python repositories and mini-swe-agent harness; post-training on three open-weight actors only; other languages and larger actors untested; no wall-clock latency or energy; how memory should be accumulated and refreshed over long repository histories is future work. Ethics: memory may retain paths, commands, test output; should follow access control, redact secrets
